items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 1 at 2:43PM AKDT until October 1 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations up to two inches.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Overall snowfall rates will be diminishing
this evening. Most of the additional snowfall will be between MP
205 and MP 235 on the Richardson Highway.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp; Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 2:40PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow continue through Friday night before gradually
drying on Saturday. An additional 1 to 2 inches of
snowfall is still possible with overall storm total snowfall
ranging from 2 to 4 inches. Isolated locations under any
persistent heavier snow may see up to 6 inches total.

Winds will be strongest Thursday night into Friday from Nuiqsut
to Kaktovik. Wind gusts will be up to 30 mph which may result in
areas of blowing/drifting snow, lowering visibility at times.
items.areas: Northern Arctic Coast; Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast

items.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 2:34PM AKDT until October 3 at 7:45AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
The second release from Suicide Basin is ongoing. Based on an
observed earlier start time of water draining from the basin, the
crest time for the Mendenhall Lake and River has been adjusted to
early Friday morning. Minor to moderate flooding continues to be
expected near Mendenhall Lake and River Thursday night into Friday
morning.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Dri
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 7:58PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
With widespread colder weather across the Interior, another front
will bring light snow to portions of the area Wednesday night
through Thursday. Generally, around 1 to 3 inches are expected
around the Central & eastern Interior, generally from around the
Fairbanks Metro Area & eastward, although some isolated locations
could receive some locally marginally higher amounts, like toward
the Chena Recreational Area, Chena Hot Springs, the White
Mountains, & Fortymile Country. Take extra precautions
items.areas: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Fortymile Country; Upper Chena River Valley; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow continue through Friday night before gradually
drying on Saturday. Between Wednesday and Friday, snowfall totals
will range from 2 to 4 inches. Isolated locations under any
persistent heavier snow may see up to 6 inches.

Winds will be strongest today near Utqiagvik (Barrow) then weaken
tomorrow, but strongest Thursday night into Friday from Nuiqsut
to Kaktovik. Wind gusts will be up to 30 mph which may result in
areas of blowing/drifting snow, lowering visibility at times.
items.areas: Northern Arctic Coast; Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
